benefits.name: Property Tax Exemption for Disabled Veterans
benefits.description: Under Arizona law, the property of a veteran with a 100% service-connected VA disability rating is fully exempt from property tax; a 2026 statutory amendment (effective Feb. 12, 2026, applying to tax years beginning Jan. 1, 2026) clarifies this full exemption covers the veteran's primary residence and continues for a non-remarried surviving spouse. Veterans with a lower service-connected rating, or a non-service-connected disability, receive a partial exemption equal to a maximum statutory dollar amount multiplied by their disability percentage, subject to household income and total-assessed-property-value limits. The exact current-year dollar figures for the partial exemption, income limit, and assessed-value cap are adjusted periodically by the Legislature and were not confirmed with certainty this session — one azleg.gov bill summary cited $4,476 as the tax-year-2025 maximum partial exemption, while other unofficial sources cite different 2026 figures; consult your County Assessor for the current-year numbers.
benefits.value: Full exemption of primary residence for veterans with a 100% VA service-connected disability rating (tax year 2026+); partial exemption for lower ratings equal to a statutory maximum amount (reported as $4,476 for tax year 2025) multiplied by disability percentage, subject to income/asset limits

otherReqs: Property must be the veteran's primary residence for the full 100%-rating exemption
Household income limits apply to the partial exemption for lower ratings (exact current-year figure not confirmed)
Total assessed property value limit applies to the partial exemption for lower ratings (exact current-year figure not confirmed)

application.agency: County Assessor (local administration); Arizona Department of Revenue
documentation: VA Summary of Benefits Letter showing disability rating

benefits.name: Arizona State Veteran Homes
benefits.description: Arizona operates four state veteran nursing homes providing skilled-nursing and long-term care, located in Phoenix, Tucson, Yuma, and Flagstaff (the newest, opened in 2024). These are administered by the Arizona Department of Veterans' Services. Specific admission criteria, cost/payment structure (e.g., VA per diem, Medicaid, private pay), and whether spouses are eligible could not be independently confirmed this session because dvs.az.gov blocked automated page retrieval (HTTP 403) on every attempt; confirm current admission requirements and costs directly with ADVS or the individual home before relying on them.

otherReqs: Details of admission criteria not independently confirmed via direct source fetch this session

benefits.name: Purple Heart Recipient Tuition Waiver Scholarship
benefits.description: Arizona law requires public universities under the Arizona Board of Regents, and community colleges, to provide a tuition waiver scholarship to Purple Heart recipients who were Arizona residents (or were stationed in Arizona) at the time of the injury that resulted in the Purple Heart, and whose VA disability rating is 50% or more. The waiver is capped at 64 credit hours at a community college, and at the number of credits needed for a baccalaureate degree at a university, and is verified by the Arizona Department of Veterans' Services.
benefits.value: Tuition waiver at Arizona public universities and community colleges, up to statutory credit-hour caps

otherReqs: Arizona resident, or stationed in Arizona, at the time of the injury
VA disability rating of 50% or more
Not convicted of a class 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 felony
Verification by the Arizona Department of Veterans' Services required

application.agency: Arizona Board of Regents / Arizona community college districts; verified by Arizona Department of Veterans' Services
documentation: ADVS verification of Purple Heart status and disability rating

benefits.name: Veteran and Disabled Veteran Hiring Preference (State Employment)
benefits.description: Arizona adds a 5-point preference to the passing civil-service exam score of honorably-discharged veterans with more than six months of active duty, for state and political-subdivision merit-system jobs. Veterans with a service-connected disability, or who receive VA or military disability compensation/retirement benefits, receive a 10-point preference instead. The statutory maximum preference is 10 points.
benefits.value: 5-point exam-score preference for veterans; 10-point preference for disabled veterans (statutory maximum 10 points)

otherReqs: More than six months of active duty for the standard 5-point preference
Service-connected disability, or receipt of VA/military disability compensation or disability retirement benefits, for the 10-point preference
Applies to external candidates taking a state or political-subdivision merit-system examination

application.agency: Arizona Department of Administration, Human Resources Division
documentation: VA disability rating letter (for disabled veteran preference)

benefits.name: Veteran License Plate
benefits.description: Arizona MVD issues a Veteran specialty license plate to veterans (and certain immediate family members of a veteran plate holder), with an optional disability symbol available at no extra charge. The plate costs $25 to initially issue and $25 annually to renew; $17 of each fee benefits a state fund supporting Arizona veterans.
benefits.value: $25 initial issuance fee; $25 annual renewal; optional disability symbol at no extra charge

otherReqs: Must have the Veteran designation on an Arizona driver license/ID, or provide DD214/215/2 (retired)/2 (reserve)/1173/256A, a statement of honorable service from the VA or Arizona Dept. of Veterans' Services, or a qualifying veteran-organization membership card

application.agency: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division (MVD)
documentation: DD214/215/2 (retired)/2 (reserve)/1173/256A, or VA/ADVS statement of honorable service, or veteran-organization membership card, or active/inactive military ID

benefits.name: Vehicle License Tax Exemption for 100% Disabled Veterans
benefits.description: A veteran who is certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as having a 100% disability and is drawing compensation on that basis is exempt from paying the vehicle license tax and registration fee on one vehicle. The exemption continues for a surviving spouse until the spouse remarries or dies, and transfers to a replacement vehicle.
benefits.value: Full waiver of vehicle license tax and registration fee on one vehicle

otherReqs: Certified 100% disabled by the U.S. Dept. of Veterans Affairs and drawing compensation on that basis
Applies to only one vehicle owned or co-owned by the veteran (or its replacement)

application.agency: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division (MVD)
documentation: VA letter of eligibility, or DoD/Uniformed Services ID card noting 100% Disabled American Veteran affiliation

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing License
benefits.description: Arizona Game and Fish Department is reported to offer a free lifetime combination hunting/fishing license to veterans with a 100% permanent-and-total VA disability rating who have held Arizona residency for at least one year, with a reduced-fee license for veterans with a lower disability rating and for Purple Heart recipients. This could not be independently confirmed this session because azgfd.com blocked automated page retrieval (HTTP 403); confirm current fees and eligibility rules directly with AZGFD before relying on them.

otherReqs: Details not independently confirmed via direct source fetch this session
